notes: Extracted 29 October 2026 from the guide (src/guides/listgroup.guide.tsx) and docs/evidence/listgroup.md at 267077a (“docs: add List Group guide”). This replaces the undocumented entry from 0.1.78+2 (a JSDoc summary and one example that set Color Mode): ListGroup now has a designer guide. The guide’s Sources note and the evidence were checked on 28 October 2026 on the installed build itself (jfs-components 0.1.78, mirror v0.1.78-dbe0e02, Biscuit’s main at dbe0e02, 27 October; the evidence says installed and upstream ListGroup.tsx are byte-identical), so items citing them carry 2026-10-28 and 0.1.78-dbe0e02. Installed ListGroup.tsx still matches every guide and evidence sentence used here, read from source, not run (token values through the package’s own getVariableByName): the root is a View, column, alignItems stretch, width 100%, background and border transparent (listGroup/background rgba(255,255,255,0), border colour hard-coded transparent, borderWidth 0), no padding (lines 408-429); the label defaults to empty and renders only when set, on one line (resolveTruncation(disableTruncation, 1)), with listGroup/gap below it only when there are rows (lines 401, 502-511); Title Level Default resolves to 14 px, weight 500, #24262b, Bold to 18 px, weight 900, #0d0d0f (line height 20, raised to 22 by safeTextLineHeight); listGroup/gap is 12 in List Item Style Default and Boxed and 4 in Minimal; in static mode listGroupSlot then children are flattened (only valid elements survive, so strings vanish) and cloned with the group’s modes, the row’s own modes merged last (react-utils cloneChildrenWithModes: { ...modes, ...existingModes }), so a row’s own modes win (lines 462-474); reorder mode starts only when data is an array and renderItem, onDragEnd and keyExtractor are functions (isReorderMode, lines 75-82), otherwise the static branch renders no rows, so only the label shows; in reorder mode renderItem’s rows are wrapped in an Animated.View and never given the group’s modes (ReorderBody, lines 221-377), the pan only activates after drag() is called from the row’s drag handle (lines 294-318), and onDragEnd gets { data, from, to } on release when the row moved (lines 276-288); accessibilityLabel is destructured out and the root gets accessibilityLabel undefined, role list, and the label Text is accessibilityElementsHidden and importantForAccessibility no (lines 488-509). ListItem’s List Item Style tokens (resolved with Context ListItem, which ListItem forces) give Default a transparent row with no padding, Boxed a white row with a #ebebed border, radius 12 and 12 px padding, Minimal titles at weight 400 (Default and Boxed 700), matching the guide’s “white card” and “lighter titles”. One guide sentence reads wider than the installed source and is not used: States “Give the group data, renderItem, keyExtractor, and onDragEnd, and every row gets a drag handle.” The group adds no handle (ReorderRow, lines 163-210, is a plain Animated.View); the handle is ListItem’s isDraggable with onDragHandleGrant={drag}, which renderItem has to set, as the evidence says and the guide’s own code does. The rule on all four props rests on the next sentence (“All four are needed”), the reorder example on the drag sentence, and the handle rule on the evidence. Not recorded as gaps, per the pack’s rules: the missing screen-reader name and the rows that aren’t list items (#420; kept as an accessibility item from the Sources note), and the MDX’s claims that accessibilityLabel names the group and rows expose listitem (evidence Discrepancies). Gaps hold what the evidence and Sources state Coin does differently: Figma’s “March 2025” title against no label by default, Code Connect not mapping the Title to label, the hard-coded transparent border against listGroup/border/color, and, from #420 (Component Bug, Component Fix › To do, Mr. Biscuit), reorder mode’s silent fall-through to the label and its missing mode cascade. Generated facts type data, keyExtractor, renderItem and onDragEnd as “undefined” (the static branch of the props union); their evidence facts say how reorder mode uses them, and the reorder example shows the real types. Examples follow the building rules: no Color Mode (the guide sets Light on every group, row, Icon Capsule and the VStack); no List Item Style or Title Level (modes that only change the look, and no guide sentence says which content needs them; the Do “Set the style on the group” is kept as a rule); the In context VStack drops the guide’s Slot gap XL and alignHorizontal stretch (a VStack stretches by default and the group is width 100% anyway); the reorder rows carry no modes, which keeps “give every row the same modes” (none on each), and the Icon Capsule drops the guide’s AppearanceBrand Neutral (slot children carry no appearance modes; ListItem passes its modes with Context ListItem into leading), so it takes the package default look. Components without an entry: MoneyValue is kept in trailing for each payment’s amount, the row’s content in the guide’s payment rows (ListItem’s own doc names MoneyValue for trailing; as the Balance entry uses it); the guide’s Monogram Avatar in leading is left out, since Avatar has no entry and leading is optional (the rows are then shorter than the guide’s 42 px). ListItem has an undocumented entry; IconCapsule gets its entry in this same batch. Copy and data are the guide’s own (March 2025, February 2025, Netflix 12 Mar 499, Swiggy 10 Mar 320, Adani Electricity 8 Mar 1,840, Jio Fiber 28 Feb 999, Zomato 14 Feb 650; Pinned on home with Savings, Bills, Mobile recharge and Wallet and their icons, all in the installed icon registry; the long label); press and drag-end handlers are stubs, so the reorder example’s screen state is left to the caller. Left out of examples (three at most): the Configuration cards (Boxed, Minimal, Title Level Bold, No label), A month and A sentence, the order readout (“Order: …”, a docs line), the playground, and the Don’ts. Not recorded: style, testID, accessibilityHint and the other View props (the guide doesn’t cover them; the building rules keep style off Coin components), listGroupSlot beyond the children fact (the evidence’s Limits keep it and children apart), onDragUpdate, the evidence’s 328 × 126 web measurement and Storybook story ids. Content bad is empty: the guide’s long label is shown to demonstrate truncation and wrapping, not marked as a Don’t. The Sources note renders whole: its code elements (jfs-components, 0.1.78, label, accessibilityLabel) appear in the rendered paragraph.

examples.purpose: Rows people can reorder, the guide’s States: data, renderItem, keyExtractor and onDragEnd are all given; each row is a ListItem with a drag handle (isDraggable, onDragHandleGrant from drag, isDragging while it is the dragged row). onDragEnd (a stub here) hands your screen the new order to save, and data is that order. The group passes no modes in this mode, and no row sets any, so every row has the same.
examples.jsx:
<ListGroup
  label="Pinned on home"
  data={[
    { id: 'Savings', title: 'Savings', support: 'Balance and statements', icon: 'ic_savings' },
    { id: 'Bills', title: 'Bills', support: 'Electricity, water, gas', icon: 'ic_bill' },
    { id: 'Mobile recharge', title: 'Mobile recharge', support: 'Jio prepaid', icon: 'ic_mobile' },
    { id: 'Wallet', title: 'Wallet', support: 'JioPay wallet', icon: 'ic_wallet' },
  ]}
  keyExtractor={(item) => item.id}
  onDragEnd={() => {}}
  renderItem={({ item, isActive, drag }) => (
    <ListItem
      layout="Horizontal"
      title={item.title}
      supportText={item.support}
      navArrow={false}
      isDraggable
      isDragging={isActive}
      onDragHandleGrant={drag}
      leading={<IconCapsule iconName={item.icon} />}
    />
  )}
/>

evidenceFacts.name: label
evidenceFacts.description: None by default. Shown above the rows on one line with an ellipsis; disableTruncation lets it wrap. 12 px (listGroup/gap) below it when there are rows.
evidenceFacts.quote: `label` (`''`): heading above the rows, one line with an ellipsis; `disableTruncation` lets it wrap.

evidenceFacts.name: children
evidenceFacts.description: The rows, stacked full width, 12 px apart. children or listGroupSlot (listGroupSlot’s rows first when both). Only elements survive: strings vanish.

evidenceFacts.name: modes
evidenceFacts.description: The group passes them to every row ({ ...group, ...row }, so a row’s own modes win), and List Items pass them on to their slots. Not in reorder mode: rows aren’t given the group’s modes there.
evidenceFacts.quote: the group passes them to every row (`{ ...group, ...row }`, so a row's own modes win)

evidenceFacts.name: List Item Style
evidenceFacts.description: Default: rows 42 px tall, no fill, 12 px gap. Boxed: rows get 12 px padding, a white fill, a 1 px #ebebed border and radius 12 (68 px tall), gap 12. Minimal: gap 4 and regular-weight titles. The look comes from List Item; the group only changes its gap.
evidenceFacts.quote: The look comes from List Item; the group only changes its gap.

evidenceFacts.name: Title Level
evidenceFacts.description: Default: the label is 14/18 medium #24262b. Bold: 18/22 black #0d0d0f.
evidenceFacts.quote: `Title Level` Default: label 14/18 Medium `#24262b`. Bold: 18/22 Black `#0d0d0f`.

evidenceFacts.name: data
evidenceFacts.description: Reorder mode: the rows’ items, with keyExtractor, renderItem and onDragEnd. All four, or the group silently renders only the label. Rows aren’t given the group’s modes in this mode.
evidenceFacts.quote: `data`, `keyExtractor`, `renderItem`, and `onDragEnd` (all four, or it silently renders only the label)

evidenceFacts.name: renderItem
evidenceFacts.description: Reorder mode: returns each row. Each row shows a drag handle (List Item isDraggable, onDragHandleGrant={drag}).
evidenceFacts.quote: Each row shows a drag handle (List Item `isDraggable`, `onDragHandleGrant={drag}`)

evidenceFacts.name: onDragEnd
evidenceFacts.description: Reorder mode: gets the new order on release; the screen saves it.
evidenceFacts.quote: `onDragEnd` gets the new order and the screen saves it.

evidenceFacts.name: accessibilityLabel
evidenceFacts.description: Dropped: the root is a list with no name, and the label text is hidden from screen readers (#420).
evidenceFacts.quote: `accessibilityLabel` is dropped; the root is `ul[role=list]` with no name, and the label text is hidden from screen readers.

gaps.text: Figma shows a “March 2025” title; the package (and Storybook’s Default) has no label until you pass one.
gaps.quote: Figma shows a "March 2025" title; the package and Storybook's Default have no label until you pass one.

gaps.text: Code Connect maps Figma’s List Group, but not its Title to label.
gaps.quote: Code Connect maps it, but not the Title to `label`.

gaps.text: The listGroup/border/color token exists, but the code hard-codes a transparent border.
gaps.quote: `listGroup/border/color` exists but the code hard-codes a transparent border.

gaps.text: Static mode passes the group’s modes to its rows; reorder mode doesn’t (Component Bug #420).
gaps.quote: Static mode passes modes to rows; reorder mode doesn't.
